title: Prevent unbounded client retry amplification and RPC deadlocks
creator: Lena Park
description:
Summary: Multiple customer escalations in February exposed a cascading failure mode where client SDKs interpreted backend transient errors as retryable without observing server-provided throttling signals. This led to request amplification and RPC deadlocks at edge-proxy -> host-router -> model-worker boundaries in hosted mode. The issue affects Hosted primarily but has a theoretically similar surface in Dedicated when proxy admission is configured.

Observed behavior:
- Customers saw repeated 5xx / long timeouts for critical calls during tenant surges.
- SDKs continued aggressive retries (no jitter, no max in some older SDK versions) causing in-flight queue saturation.
- Edge proxy started queuing requests per tenant which prevented forward progress; KV cache eviction thrashing happened as workers starved for CPU, amplifying tail latency and 5xx errors.
- Some Private deployments with older router configs hit similar stalls in lab repros.

Root cause hypothesis:
- Two contributing defects: (1) server returned heterogeneous errors (mix of 429/503/502/504) but did not set consistent Retry-After or idempotency guidance; (2) older SDKs treat all 5xx as retryable and use a high maxRetries with no global concurrency cap.
- A secondary issue: our proxy's admission control lacked a tenant-scoped inflight cap tied to observed downstream error rate, so retries queued rather than shed.

Repro steps (internal):
1. Use load generator with 1. spike to 10x normal RPS for target tenant, 2. use legacy SDK client config (maxRetries=50, no jitter), 3. target short sequence long-latency model (L seq=1024) to trigger KV churn.
2. Observe Grafana: tenant inflight queue length climbs, worker CPU saturates, 5xx rate increases, and graph of retries-per-request shows exponential amplification.

Proposed mitigation plan:
- Short term (hotfix): server will add explicit Retry-After or X-Retryable-Type headers for transient throttling (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/13421). Add a lightweight tenant-scoped inflight cap at edge-proxy (default 200) to shed and return clear 429 with Retry-After when exceeded. Deploy to canary region for 24h.
- Medium term: update hosted API to emit standardized guidance headers and implement adaptive tenant backpressure that ties allowed inflight to observed worker success ratio.
- Long term: SDKs will be updated to default to conservative retry policies (maxRetries=4, exponential backoff, jitter, respect Retry-After). Provide a compatibility shim in the proxy to translate legacy SDK retry patterns into server-side pacing when possible.

Rollout strategy:
- Hotfix: canary -> region us-east-1 -> global over 48 hours with 2h observation windows. Emergency fast rollback path: toggle edge-proxy inflight cap to unlimited via runtime flag.
- SDK changes: publish new SDK minor that is opt-in for 2 weeks, then opt-out before broad enforcement. Coordinate customer comms and release notes.

Testing & validation:
- Unit tests for header emission and proxy-shed behavior included in PR.
- Stress test harness reproducer in QA (link below) and synthetic tenant surge replay to assert amplification reduced by >=90%.
- Add dashboard panels for per-tenant retries-per-request, inflight-queue-length, and retry amplification ratio. Set alerts at 10x baseline.

Monitoring & runbook updates:
- Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.internal.redwood/company/tenant-retries (new panels added).
- Incident runbook updated: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Retry+Amplification+Runbook
- PagerDuty play: escalation to SRE -> servicing-runtime team if per-tenant retry amplification > 5 for 5min.

Backward compatibility & customer comms:
- For tenants on older SDKs, proxy will translate Retry-After into a client-visible header where possible and emit more explicit 429 messages. Outreach to top impacted customers planned this week, with suggested SDK patch and mitigation steps.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- What default inflight cap per-tenant balances latency vs fairness? (proposal: 200 normal, 50 low-tier).
- How aggressive should server-side pacing be for legacy clients to avoid breaking idempotency semantics?
- Should we auto-upgrade some SDKs server-side via feature-flagged behavior? Security and consent implications need review.

Artifacts:
- Reproducer harness (QA job): https://ci.redwood.ai/job/retry-amplification-repro/324
- Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/13421
- Proxy admission shim PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/902
comments: 2026-02-11 - Lena Park: Initial incident triage. Captured heap profiles and inflight queue traces. Noticed disproportionate retries per request for tenant T-239.
2026-02-14 - Miguel Torres: Confirmed repro in staging with legacy SDK. Began prototyping inflight cap in edge-proxy. Added initial metrics export for retries-per-request.
2026-02-20 - Priya Natarajan (SRE): Deployed proxy canary with inflight cap=200 to us-west-2; observed 78% reduction in retry amplification after 3h. Filed PR for canary rollout.
2026-03-02 - Design Review (PM/Eng): Agreed on header standard X-RW-Retry-Type and consistent use of Retry-After. PM to draft customer messaging.
2026-03-08 - Security: Reviewed no sensitive data in new headers. Ok to ship. Security notes: ensure rate-limit logs are redacted for PII.
2026-03-12 - Miguel Torres: Merged hotfix PR, started canary deployment to us-east-1. Monitoring alerts configured. Next: schedule SDK advisory and customer outreach.
